task: Stop an implementer who also dispatches from supplying the session identity that a topology critic signs its receipt under.
outcome: topology_critic_receipt_set refuses any session whose identity did not come from a host adapter, so a critic receipt is evidence of an independent actor rather than of a string the implementer chose.
facts: independenceMatrix (packages/main/src/core/topology-critic-receipt.ts:181-188) establishes independence with four textual !== comparisons between actor and implementation provenance.
Neither deriveRoleProvenance nor deriveImplementationProvenance checks who originated an identity; both read sessionId off the most recent matching ProcessEvent on disk.

deriveRoleProvenance requires a dispatch event whose sessionId equals the signer's own session id, and dispatch is not in the critic's allowedCommandIds (prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:300), so a correctly sandboxed critic cannot satisfy it unaided.
resolveSessionIdentity classifies every session by sessionSource: host-adapter, explicit-env, generated-token, or derived-ppid.

host-adapter session ids are hash-derived by deriveAdapterOwnerSessionId from projectRoot, provider, task identity and agent identity, so they cannot be freely chosen; explicit-env is whatever was placed in LATTICE_SESSION_ID.

The bypass was demonstrated live during B-3f3d: a dispatch event was recorded under an implementer-chosen session id and passed every mechanical check. An independent critic refused to adopt the session; that refusal is currently the only thing preventing a self-signed receipt.
LATTICE_SESSION_ID appears on 167 lines (170 occurrences; 3 lines carry it twice) across 29 files under packages/main/src/tasks.

Commit 9f9f53a514 (B-3f3d) moved the acceptance-basis requirement off an unconditional throw onto the pass branch only, so request_changes tolerates a stale basis while pass still requires a verified one.
A prototype of the guard was written during B-3f3d, confirmed to refuse explicit-env correctly, then reverted because the test migration is too large to carry inline.

Investigated: the 29 test files use LATTICE_SESSION_ID uniformly (67 direct process.env assignments plus save/restore pairs and a few env-object literals). No bespoke identity construction was found, so one shared adapter-session helper is viable.

Investigated: generated-token sessions pass through the SAME provider + task + agent gate as host-adapter (owner-session-adapters.ts:160-173) and additionally require a boundary token, so they are equally host-derived and equally unmintable by an implementer. The prototype refusing them was over-strict.

Investigated: deriveRoleProvenance has exactly two non-test callers, both in packages/main/src/handlers/proofstory.ts. Line 550 binds TOPOLOGY_EXCLUSION_APPROVER_ROLE (scope-plan approver) and line 565 binds TOPOLOGY_CRITIC_ROLE.
constraints: The guard must not block legitimate dispatched critics. Blocking everything would satisfy the negative tests while making BUG-CRITIC-DISPATCH-PROVENANCE-UNSATISFIABLE worse.
PASS must not become reachable on a stale basis; the 9f9f53a514 asymmetry must survive unchanged.
No CLI amends a created story's title or description, and editing .lattice/story metadata directly is forbidden (CLAUDE.md rule 8).
Normal channel: the main agent does not write business code; lattice-implementer subagents do.
Security/Credentials riskSignal is active and deliberately not dismissed, so decision_set requires at least 3 preMortem entries.
unknowns: Whether to accept generated-token alongside host-adapter. Evidence favours accepting both since both are host-derived; the decision belongs in decision_set rather than being assumed here.
